finding.claim: getRedirectUrl turns a request path with a leading dot segment into a protocol-relative Location header, so a directory request can redirect to an attacker-chosen host. Severity low, verdict PLAUSIBLE. Precondition: redirect: true is set (opt-in, index.js:317) and the path resolves to a directory under root. The host is limited to names of existing directories in the served tree.
finding.source: Raw request target req.raw.url, e.g. GET /.//css (attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: reply.redirect(getRedirectUrl(request.raw.url), 301) at index.js:319 sets the Location header.

trace.note: Wildcard handler passes req.raw.url to getPathnameForSend.
Returns '/.//css'. The '..' test does not match a single '.' segment.
opts.redirect === true, so the redirect branch runs.
getRedirectUrl(request.raw.url) is called on the raw URL.
url = '/' + './/css' = '/.//css' after stripping the single leading slash.
new URL('/.//css', 'http://localhost.com/'): the '.' segment is dropped, leaving an empty first segment, so pathname = '//css'.
Appends '/', returning '//css/'. Location: //css/ is protocol-relative and points to host 'css'.

finding.guards_checked: Leading slash/backslash stripping (index.js:786-790) only handles slashes at the start of the URL, not slashes after a dot segment. Only parsedPathname and search are returned, so a host in the host position is dropped; this blocks the naive '//evil.com' case but not '/.//host'. No check that the result does not start with '//'. Dot-dot guards (index.js:262, 769) look only for '..', not '.'. Host set is limited to existing directory names, which caps practical impact. Fix: collapse leading slashes after normalization (e.g. replace /^\/+/ with '/' on parsedPathname) or reject results starting with '//'. Verified by reading against WHATWG URL parsing rules; not executed (no shell tool available).

finding.claim: With list.extendedFolderInfo enabled, each directory listing request walks the full subtree of every listed subdirectory with no caching, depth limit or symlink-cycle check. Severity low, verdict PLAUSIBLE. Precondition: operator enables list with extendedFolderInfo (opt-in); symlinks inside root are operator-controlled.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET of a listed directory (e.g. the root).
finding.sink: dirList._getExtendedInfo (lib/dirList.js:25-51) recursively calls fs.stat (which follows symlinks) and readdir on every subdirectory.

trace.note: Directory listing triggered for a directory request.
extendedFolderInfo: getExtendedInfo runs for each directory entry.
Unbounded recursion into subdirectories; fs.stat follows symlinks, so cycles recurse until PATH_MAX/ELOOP.

finding.guards_checked: Option is opt-in; default is off. Errors are caught in dirList.list's caller (dirList.js:132), so no error details leak. fastq concurrency is bounded, but total work is not bounded.
